annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ciofu, I.A.; Caraiani, C.; Pelau, C.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot classifications are blurring as technologies converge into multifunctional, socially interactive agents.
Anthropomorphic design raises user trust, engagement, emotional attachment and acceptance.
Ethical risks include emotional manipulation, stereotype reinforcement and psychological dependence.
Successful integration needs ethical, context-aware design aligned with social expectations.
Calls for responsible, human-empowered innovation and multidisciplinary approaches.
annotation.summary_en: Structured literature review of robot types (social, educational, entertainment, industrial, collaborative, mobile, service, humanoid) and how anthropomorphic design shapes human-robot interaction, trust and acceptance. It flags ethical risks such as emotional manipulation, stereotypes and dependence, and urges context-aware, responsible design rather than proposing specific regulation.
annotation.title_clean: Robots in Society: Design, Functionality, and Ethical Challenges in Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.title_en: Robots in Society: Design, Functionality, and Ethical Challenges in Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.venue: 11th BASIQ International Conference on New Trends in Sustainable Business and Consumption
